cost: THE SUBJECT LANDS AT 87 AGAINST A STATED 88, INSIDE HIS +-3 BUT ON THE LOW HALF, AND THE REASON IS A CONSTANT THIS FILE SPENDS ELSEWHERE. His whole perimeter vector is 80.72 x 1.1305 = 91.3, so 88 exactly needs him about 0.35 big, i.e. a ramp top near 76 rather than 68. Every top above DET_LO is a NEW constant — the file's own statements about where a rim claim is whole are 45 (a claim begins), 55 (recal_136's saturation), 68 (recal_99's deterrence foot) and 80 (clause 3's absolute bar); 80 as the top reads McCray 89 but takes Dennis Rodman '96 to 0.17 big and OVR 67, one outside his 63 +-3. 68 is the last existing constant that holds every pin, and 87 is what it pays.

DENNIS RODMAN '96 IS THE STOPPING PIN AND HE IS ON HIS EDGE. ovr 63 +-3, reading 66 (DEF 87 -> 89) at rimprot 51 / perdef 94. Any widening of this ramp's top past DET_LO, or any lowering of its foot, moves him first. A later round that wants McCray on 88 exactly is asking for that pin to be released.

THE FLAT 45->68 TOP THE SCOUT MEASURED IS SUPERSEDED BY THE GATED ONE, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS 58 CARDS. Flat: 200 cards in the band, 53 rise >= 3, 62 FALL >= 3 (LaPhonso Ellis '94/'98, Walter Berry '87/'88, Michael Kidd-Gilchrist '13 at -8 and -9). Gated on the lead perdef has over rimprot: 41 rise >= 3 and FOUR fall >= 3, all at exactly -3. The men who fell under the flat form move by ZERO under this one, by construction, and that is the form the dispatch asked to be considered.

THREE TACTICS TAXES WERE RE-RATIFIED AND THE INTEGRATOR MUST RE-SWEEP FROM MAIN'S CONSTANTS, NOT FROM THESE. hunt 3.65 -> 3.74, crashOff 0.28 -> 0.13, crashDef 0.60 -> 0.30. hunt's window this time is 0.023 wide, the narrowest it has ever recorded; crashOff's own interval has a NEGATIVE midpoint for the second time in the file's history (r117 was the first), so it took the positive half's midpoint.
DEF_TOP WAS NOT RE-DERIVED (the dispatch forbade it) and nothing this round moves sits above the knee: the whole footprint is under 93 raw. The top 12 by DEF is identical, card for card.
notes: WHAT THE DEFECT IS, DECOMPOSED ON THE SUBJECT. Rodney McCray '88 — 1988 All-Defensive FIRST team, 33.2 mpg, 6'7" (height 79) — has perdef 93, discipline 93, rimprot 56, drb 57, perimdisrupt 12 (as shipped; recal_181's lockdown floor pays it as 48.73 inside the perimeter half). His listing is ['SF','PF'], so recal_103's POSITION branch decides him and never reaches a shape clause. recal_103's own override cannot see him: his perimdisrupt-minus-drb gap is -45, the rebounding side of the test, because he is a low-event stopper rather than a ball-hawk. recal_187's rim-presence ramp saturates at 55 and his rimprot is 56 — ONE POINT past it — so it releases nothing either. He was graded 1.000 big: 0.40 x 93 + 0.40 x 56 + 0.17 x 57 = 72.0, against his own perimeter vector of 80.7, and printed DEF 81, #19 of 1988.

WHY THE TOP IS THE KNOB AND NOT THE FOOT. recal_187 borrowed BOTH ends of its ramp from recal_136, which set them for a different question. The foot (45, where a rim-protection claim begins) is right for this question too and is untouched — that is why Carroll '14, Crowder '16 and Ingles '17, recal_187's own three subjects, move by exactly zero. The TOP is the guess: 55 is where recal_136 said a man who does not shoot is WHOLLY a big, and it leaves a 6'7" wing with rimprot 56-67 graded entirely on a big vector while recal_99's deterrence clause — the file's other statement about a whole rim claim — does not think that number deters anybody until 68.

WHY THE TOP IS A FUNCTION AND NOT A CONSTANT, WHICH IS THE ROUND'S ONE REAL CHOICE. Moving the top flat to 68 is right for a wing whose perimeter defence is his case (McCray, Wallace, Covington) and WRONG for a listed power forward whose rim number is his case: LaPhonso Ellis '94 (rimprot 64 > perdef 61), Walter Berry '88 (65 > 47), Kidd-Gilchrist '13 (62 > 50) each lose eight or nine points to it, and they should lose nothing — their listing and their sheet AGREE. So the top is set by the SIGNED LEAD perdef has over rimprot, over recal_164's own width 10, the quantity every other clause in this function already reads. At lead 0 the branch is byte-identical to recal_187; at lead 10 the top is DET_LO. NO NEW CONSTANT ENTERS THE FILE.

THE CLASS, AND IT IS WHY THIS IS A FORMULA AND NOT A CARD. The dispatch named two more instances and both are the same shape — wing height, a real but unremarkable rim number, a perimeter sheet nobody was grading them on. Gerald Wallace '12 (perdef 90, rimprot 57) 81 -> 86, with '13 78 -> 84 and '14 76 -> 82. Robert Covington '17 (perdef 96, rimprot 64) 85 -> 87, with '16 78 -> 83 and '15 76 -> 80 — he releases LEAST of the three because his rim number is the highest, which is the ramp doing exactly what it says. The largest movers on the whole board are the same archetype recal_103 named: Luc Mbah a Moute '16 +10, George McGinnis '82 +8, Chuck Hayes '08 +6, Rodney Rogers '03 +5, Eduardo Nájera '08 +5, Chris Singleton '12 +5.

THE FOUR FALLERS ARE NOT A DEFECT, THEY ARE THE SAME SENTENCE READ THE OTHER WAY. Andrés Nocioni '06/'07, Buck Williams '88 and Miles Bridges '26 each have perdef ahead of rimprot, so the branch releases them toward their own perimeter vector — and for them that vector is LOWER than the big one. All four move exactly -3, and Buck Williams '88 is the clearest reading of it: a rebounding power forward at perdef 64 no longer outscores an All-Defensive first-team wing on defence (76 against 87, where it was 79 against 81).

OFF AND EVERY ATTRIBUTE MOVE ON ZERO CARDS. is_big is untouched, exactly as recal_93 / recal_103 / recal_164 / recal_187 left it, so the boolean still labels the card, still gates recal_55's big hub and recal_91's stretch-big floor, and still picks the OVR cap branch. Only d_score's mix weight moves: 217 DEF (154 up, 63 down, max +10 / -3) and 133 OVR (max +6 / -2) of 10,000.
